checklist.step: Pull the market-level premium and claims population for the reporting period
actions: In the actuarial modeling platform open the MLR data model and refresh the claims and premium extract from the enterprise data warehouse for the individual-market block, split by state.
Filter to earned premium and incurred claims transactions dated within the MLR reporting year, including run-out claims paid after period end.
Ask the Data Analyst to confirm the extract row count matches the source claims system's period-end control total.
Save the reconciled extract to the MLR workpaper folder named <state>-<market>-<year>-source-extract.
checklist.done: the premium and claims extract is refreshed, filtered to the reporting year and reconciled to the source system control total for every state.

checklist.step: Build the MLR numerator per 45 CFR 158.140
actions: Sum incurred claims, plus the fraud-recovery, ICD-10, and HIT adjustments 158.140 permits, into the numerator workpaper tab.
Add allowed quality-improvement activity expense per the 158.150 definition, tagging each expense line with its QIA category.
Exclude any expense the regulation excludes (e.g., non-QIA administrative cost) and note the exclusion basis on the row.
Total the numerator by state and market and cross-cast to the source extract to confirm no claims lines were dropped.
checklist.done: the numerator workpaper totals incurred claims plus allowed QIA expense by state/market, cross-cast to the source extract.

checklist.step: Build the MLR denominator per 45 CFR 158.150
actions: Total earned premium by state and market from the extract.
Deduct federal and state taxes, licensing and regulatory fees permitted under 158.161, itemizing each deduction on its own row with the statutory basis.
Cross-check the tax and fee figures against the Tax Analyst's filed returns for the same period.
Total the adjusted denominator by state/market.
checklist.done: the denominator workpaper totals adjusted earned premium by state/market with every tax/fee deduction itemized and cross-checked to filed returns.

checklist.step: Apply the credibility adjustment per 45 CFR 158.130
actions: Determine the member-life-year count for each state/market block and classify it as non-credible, partially credible or fully credible per the 158.130 table.
Apply the prescribed credibility adjustment factor and, where applicable, the deductible-factor adjustment.
Document the classification and factor applied on the workpaper with the member-life-year count that drove it.
Flag any block that crosses a credibility threshold since the prior period for extra scrutiny.
checklist.done: every state/market block carries a documented credibility classification and adjustment factor tied to its member-life-year count.

checklist.step: Compute the preliminary rebate percentage and reserve
actions: Compute the MLR = (credibility-adjusted numerator) / denominator for each state/market.
Compare to the applicable standard (80% individual/small group, 85% large group) and compute the shortfall where MLR is below standard per 158.240.
Apply the 158.241 rebate formula (shortfall × earned premium) to derive the aggregate rebate liability.
Divide the aggregate liability across enrollees per the prescribed per-enrollee method and record the per-enrollee average.
checklist.done: MLR, shortfall and rebate liability are computed and compared to the applicable standard for every state/market.

checklist.step: Reconcile the computation to the statutory financial statement
actions: Compare the numerator's incurred claims total to the statutory Annual Statement Underwriting and Investment Exhibit claims incurred line.
Compare the denominator's earned premium total to the statutory premium earned line for the same block.
Investigate and document any variance over 1% between the MLR workpaper and the statutory blank.
Sign off that the MLR data ties to the statutory financials before the reserve is booked.
checklist.done: numerator and denominator totals are reconciled to the statutory financial statement with variances over 1% explained and signed off.

checklist.step: Book the rebate-liability reserve
actions: Post the computed rebate-liability reserve to the designated MLR liability account in the general ledger, by state/market.
Attach the workpaper reference number to the journal entry memo field.
Have the Financial Analyst confirm the posted amount matches the workpaper total before the entry is finalized.
checklist.done: the rebate-liability reserve is posted to the general ledger by state/market and matches the workpaper total.

checklist.step: Document the methodology and assumptions memo
actions: Write a methodology memo covering data sources, numerator/denominator construction, credibility classification and any judgmental adjustments.
State the prior-period comparison and explain any methodology change.
File the memo alongside the workpaper in the MLR reserve folder.
checklist.done: a dated methodology memo covering data, construction and judgmental adjustments is filed with the workpaper.

checklist.step: Route the workpaper for peer review
actions: Independently re-foot the numerator and denominator totals and re-derive the credibility factor from the member-life-year count.
Compare the reviewer's rebate percentage to the preparer's; investigate any difference beyond rounding.
Note review comments on the workpaper and confirm each is resolved before sign-off.
checklist.done: an independent peer review of the numerator, denominator and credibility factor is documented with comments resolved.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary certification
actions: Review the workpaper, methodology memo and peer-review notes.
Certify the reserve is computed in accordance with 45 CFR Subpart B and sign the certification page.
Return unresolved items to the Appointed Actuary rather than certifying around them.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has signed a dated certification of the reserve computation.

checklist.step: Re-run the computation at each subsequent quarter-end
actions: Refresh the source extract for the newest quarter and re-run the full numerator/denominator/credibility/reserve build.
Carry forward prior-quarter figures for trend comparison on the same workpaper tab.
Route the refreshed computation through the same peer-review and certification steps.
checklist.done: each quarter's reserve is recomputed from a refreshed extract and carried through peer review and certification.

checklist.step: Explain quarter-over-quarter reserve movement
actions: Compare the current quarter's MLR and reserve to the prior quarter by state/market.
Attribute the movement to claims development, premium growth, credibility-tier changes or methodology changes.
Record the attribution on the workpaper for the Controller's quarter-end review.
checklist.done: quarter-over-quarter reserve movement is attributed by driver and recorded on the workpaper.

checklist.step: Prepare the year-end handoff package for the MLR annual report team
actions: Assemble the final numerator, denominator, credibility factor and rebate calculation for the full benefit year by state/market.
Hand the package to Regulatory Reporting with the certification memo and the reconciliation to the statutory blank.
Confirm the handoff occurs early enough for the report team to meet the July 31 HHS filing deadline.
checklist.done: the final MLR calculation package is handed to Regulatory Reporting with time to spare before July 31.

checklist.step: Log any restatement or late reserve
actions: Where a prior-period reserve is restated, open a tracker issue with the change amount, cause and affected filings.
Assess whether the restatement requires an amended MLR report and route that assessment to Regulatory Counsel.
Record the disposition and closure date on the tracker issue.
checklist.done: every restatement is logged with cause, amended-filing assessment and closure date.

checklist.step: Archive the reserve workpapers to the evidence repository
actions: Upload the final workpaper, methodology memo, peer-review notes and certification to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by state, market and reporting year.
Confirm the record is retrievable by a search on state and reporting year.
checklist.done: the complete reserve record is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by state and reporting year.

testing.step: Build the population of MLR reserve computations for the period
actions: Extract every state/market MLR reserve computation booked in the period from the actuarial modeling platform.
Reconcile the count and total booked reserve to the general ledger MLR liability account balance.
Resolve any difference between the extract and the ledger before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the general ledger MLR liability balance and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the source data to the statutory financial statement
actions: Compare the numerator and denominator source totals to the corresponding statutory Annual Statement exhibit lines.
Recompute the variance percentage and confirm it is within the 1% tolerance the procedure sets.
List any state/market where the source data does not tie as an exception.
testing.done: source data is reconciled to the statutory blank with variances over tolerance listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of state/market blocks classified as non-credible or partially credible.
Take a random sample of 8 fully-credible blocks, minimum 15 blocks total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every non/partially-credible block.

testing.step: Re-perform the numerator, denominator and credibility calculation for the sample
actions: Independently rebuild the numerator, denominator and credibility factor for each sampled block from the raw extract, without referencing the preparer's workpaper.
Compare the re-performed MLR and rebate liability to the booked figure; any variance beyond 0.1 percentage point is a fail.
Capture the re-performance calculation into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled block has an independent re-performance with the pass/fail threshold applied.

testing.step: Trace tax and fee deductions to filed returns
actions: For each sampled block, trace the 158.161 tax/fee deductions to the Tax Analyst's filed return for the same period.
Confirm the deducted amount and statutory basis match the filed return.
Flag any deduction that cannot be traced to a filed return.
testing.done: every sampled tax/fee deduction is traced to a filed return or flagged.

testing.step: Verify the credibility classification against the member-life-year count
actions: Recompute member-life-years for each sampled block from the source extract.
Compare against the 158.130 credibility table to confirm the classification and factor used were correct.
Flag any block sitting within 2% of a credibility-tier boundary for extra scrutiny.
testing.done: the credibility classification is independently verified for every sampled block.

testing.step: Trace the booked reserve to the general ledger
actions: Pull the general ledger journal entry for each sampled block's reserve.
Confirm the posted amount matches the workpaper total and carries the correct workpaper reference.
Note any unexplained difference between the workpaper and the ledger posting.
testing.done: every sampled reserve is traced to a matching general ledger posting.

testing.step: Confirm peer review and certification exist for every sampled block
actions: Check each sampled block's workpaper carries a dated peer-review note from the Reserving Actuary.
Check the Chief Actuary certification page is signed and dated before the reserve was booked.
List any block missing either sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: peer review and certification are confirmed present and correctly sequenced for every sampled block.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception with the state/market, what failed and the dollar impact.
Assign a root cause (data extract gap, wrong credibility tier, missing sign-off, tax deduction unsupported) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next test cycle as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the pass/fail threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled workpapers, sign the test workpaper.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report the result to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed test workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Assemble the rate development data package
actions: Pull the base-period claims, membership and premium experience for the individual-market block from the actuarial modeling platform.
Apply trend, benefit-change and demographic adjustment factors per the pricing methodology.
Ask the Data Analyst to confirm the base-period membership count matches the enrollment system's period-end count.
Save the reconciled data package to the rate filing workpaper folder.
checklist.done: a reconciled base-period data package with trend and adjustment factors applied is filed in the rate workpaper folder.

checklist.step: Populate the Unified Rate Review Template
actions: Open the current-year URRT workbook published by CMS and enter the base-period experience, trend factors and proposed rate change by plan.
Complete Worksheets 1 and 2 with the plan-level rate increase, projected loss ratio and membership.
Cross-check every proposed rate figure against the pricing actuary's data package for consistency.
checklist.done: the URRT is fully populated and every proposed rate ties to the underlying pricing data package.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial memorandum (Parts I-III)
actions: Draft Part I (general information), Part II (proposed rate change) and Part III (experience and projections) per the 154.215 documentation requirements.
Include the trend assumptions, benefit changes, risk-adjustment and reinsurance impacts, and administrative expense load.
Have the Pricing Actuary review the memorandum against the data package for numerical consistency.
checklist.done: the memorandum covers Parts I-III with assumptions consistent with the URRT and the underlying data package.

checklist.step: Confirm each state's specific rate filing requirements
actions: In SERFF open Industry ▸ Filing Rules for the state and select Health, Rate/Rule filing type.
Note any state-specific rate filing checklist items beyond the federal URRT/memorandum, such as a state actuarial certification form.
Confirm whether the state performs effective rate review or defers to CMS's federal review.
checklist.done: state-specific filing requirements and the review authority (state vs CMS) are recorded for each filing state.

checklist.step: Route the memorandum for internal actuarial review
actions: Independently recompute the projected loss ratio from the URRT inputs and compare to the memorandum's stated figure.
Check the trend and administrative expense assumptions against the company's most recent experience study.
Log review comments and confirm each is resolved before the memorandum moves to certification.
checklist.done: an independent internal review is documented with all comments resolved.

checklist.step: Certify and sign the actuarial memorandum
actions: Review the finalized URRT and memorandum against the 154.215 documentation checklist.
Sign the actuarial certification page attesting the rate development follows Actuarial Standards of Practice.
Date the certification and confirm it predates the SERFF/HIOS submission.
checklist.done: a dated, signed certification exists and predates submission.

checklist.step: Submit the URRT and memorandum through SERFF or the CMS Rate Review module
actions: In SERFF, create a new Rate/Rule filing for the state, attach the URRT workbook, memorandum and any state-specific certification form.
For states relying on CMS federal rate review, additionally upload the URRT to CMS's HIOS Rate Review module by the federal deadline.
Submit and record the SERFF tracking number (and HIOS confirmation number where applicable) on the rate filing log.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted with a recorded SERFF tracking number and, where applicable, a HIOS confirmation number.

checklist.step: Track the filing through review to disposition
actions: Monitor the SERFF filing status and respond to any state objection letter within the state's stated response window.
Loop in the Appointed Actuary for any objection questioning a pricing assumption.
Record the final disposition (Approved/Filed/Disapproved) and effective date on the rate filing log.
checklist.done: the filing log shows the final disposition, effective date and every objection response.

checklist.step: Reconcile the certified rates to the pricing system before go-live
actions: Compare the approved rate tables to what is configured in the rating engine.
Flag and correct any discrepancy before the plan year's effective date.
Obtain sign-off from the Product / Filing Actuary that the configured rates match the approved filing.
checklist.done: configured rates match the approved filing before the effective date, with sign-off on file.

checklist.step: Maintain the rate filing tracking log
actions: Add a row per state/product filing with submission date, certification date, tracking number and disposition.
Link each row to its workpaper folder.
Review the log monthly during filing season for stale open filings.
checklist.done: the log carries one complete, linked row per filing and is reviewed monthly during filing season.

checklist.step: Handle rate filing amendments
actions: Where CMS or a state requires a rate revision, update the URRT and memorandum to reflect the revised figures.
Route the amendment through the same internal review and Appointed Actuary certification steps as the original filing.
Resubmit through SERFF/HIOS referencing the original tracking number.
checklist.done: every amendment is re-certified and resubmitted with a reference to the original filing.

checklist.step: Escalate filings at risk of missing the deadline
actions: Compare each open filing's current status to the state's submission deadline at each T-30 checkpoint.
Escalate any filing at risk to the Chief Actuary and Chief Compliance Officer within one business day of identifying the risk.
Record the escalation decision and outcome on the filing log.
checklist.done: every at-risk filing is escalated with a recorded decision before the deadline passes.

checklist.step: Confirm SBC and consumer disclosure documents reflect the approved rate change
actions: Compare the Summary of Benefits and Coverage premium disclosures to the approved rate filing.
Update consumer-facing materials before the plan year's open enrollment publication date.
Obtain Regulatory Counsel review of the updated disclosure language.
checklist.done: consumer disclosures match the approved rates and are cleared by Regulatory Counsel before publication.

checklist.step: Log any late filing or certification gap
actions: Where a filing is submitted without a predating certification or after the state deadline, open a tracker issue.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Route to Regulatory Counsel for assessment of any required self-report.
checklist.done: every late filing or certification gap is logged with root cause, owner and a Regulatory Counsel assessment.

checklist.step: Archive the rate filing package
actions: Upload the URRT, memorandum, certification, SERFF/HIOS confirmation and disposition letter to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by state, product and filing year.
checklist.done: the complete rate filing package is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by state, product and year.

testing.step: Build the population of rate filings submitted in the plan year
actions: Extract every rate/rule filing submitted in SERFF for the plan year across all states and products.
Reconcile the extract to the internal rate filing tracking log.
Resolve any filing present in one source but not the other before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between SERFF and the internal log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each filing to a certification predating submission
actions: Match each population row to its Appointed Actuary certification date.
Confirm the certification date is earlier than the SERFF/HIOS submission date.
List unmatched or out-of-sequence rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every filing is matched to a predating certification or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of filings that drew a CMS or state objection.
Take a random sample of 10 additional filings from the remaining population, minimum 15 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every objected filing.

testing.step: Re-perform the URRT loss-ratio calculation for sampled filings
actions: Independently recompute the projected loss ratio from the URRT's underlying trend and experience inputs.
Compare to the memorandum's stated figure; any variance beyond 0.5 percentage point is a fail.
Capture the recomputation into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing has an independent loss-ratio re-performance with the pass/fail threshold applied.

testing.step: Verify the memorandum's assumptions against the experience study
actions: Compare the trend and administrative expense assumptions in each sampled memorandum to the company's contemporaneous experience study.
Flag any assumption materially inconsistent with the experience study without a documented rationale.
Note the finding in the workpaper.
testing.done: assumptions are checked against the experience study for every sampled filing, with inconsistencies flagged.

testing.step: Trace the submission to SERFF/HIOS and confirm the disposition
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, search each sampled tracking number and confirm the filed URRT/memorandum match the internal workpaper.
Confirm the disposition and effective date recorded in the log match SERFF.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing traces to a matching SERFF record with the correct disposition and effective date.

testing.step: Confirm configured rates match the approved filing
actions: For each sampled filing, compare the approved rate table to the rating engine configuration as of the effective date.
Flag any mismatch as a rate-implementation exception.
Record the comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: configured rates are verified against the approved filing for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Confirm consumer disclosure alignment
actions: Compare Summary of Benefits and Coverage premium figures for sampled filings to the approved rates.
Confirm Regulatory Counsel's disclosure review sign-off exists and predates publication.
Note any misalignment as an exception.
testing.done: consumer disclosures are confirmed aligned to approved rates for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the state, product and what failed.
Assign root cause (late certification, unsupported assumption, rate-config mismatch) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next filing season as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-tolerance certification threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and report to the Compliance Committee.
Have the independent reviewer sign the test workpaper and file it in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Route the completed form for actuarial and financial review

actions: Submit the completed form through the HHS MLR data-collection system before the July 31 statutory deadline.
Download and save the system-generated submission confirmation number and timestamp.
Notify the Controller and Appointed Actuary that the filing is complete.
checklist.done: the report is submitted before July 31 with a saved confirmation number and timestamp.

checklist.step: Log the filing on the regulatory filing calendar
actions: Record the submission date, confirmation number and filer of record on the filing calendar for every state/market.
Mark the July 31 milestone as closed for the reporting year.
Set the reminder cadence for next year's cycle.
checklist.done: the filing calendar shows the closed milestone with confirmation number for every state/market.

checklist.step: Reconcile the submitted figures back to the general ledger rebate liability
actions: Compare the rebate liability reported to HHS against the general ledger MLR liability account balance.
Investigate and resolve any variance before the next quarter's close.
Document the reconciliation in the close workpapers.
checklist.done: the submitted rebate liability is reconciled to the general ledger balance with variances resolved.

checklist.step: Prepare and issue enrollee rebates where MLR falls below standard
actions: For any state/market with a rebate due, pull the enrollee list eligible for a rebate per 158.240.
Calculate the per-enrollee rebate amount using the certified average and issue via premium credit or check per the prescribed method.
Confirm rebates are distributed by the regulatory deadline (generally September 30 following the MLR reporting year).
checklist.done: eligible enrollees receive their rebate by the statutory distribution deadline, using the certified per-enrollee amount.

checklist.step: Respond to any HHS data-validation query
actions: Monitor the HHS MLR system for any post-submission data query or validation flag.
Coordinate with the Appointed Actuary and Controller to research and answer the query within the CMS-stated response window.
Log the query and response on the filing calendar.
checklist.done: every HHS query is answered within the stated window and logged.

checklist.step: Handle any required amended MLR report
actions: Where a data error is discovered post-submission, prepare the corrected figures and route through the same actuarial/Controller/compliance review chain.
Submit the amendment through the HHS MLR system referencing the original confirmation number.
Recalculate any rebate impact and coordinate reissuance with Billing Operations.
checklist.done: any amendment is re-reviewed, resubmitted with a reference to the original filing, and any rebate impact recalculated.

checklist.step: Escalate any risk to the July 31 deadline
actions: At each T-10 checkpoint, compare data-readiness status to the deadline.
Escalate any state/market at risk to the Chief Compliance Officer and Controller within one business day.
Record the escalation and resulting decision on the filing calendar.
checklist.done: any at-risk state/market is escalated with a recorded decision before July 31.

checklist.step: Log any missed deadline or data exception
actions: Open a tracker issue for any late submission or post-submission correction.
Assign root cause and owner, and route to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report assessment where the deadline was missed.
Set a remediation date and confirm closure.
checklist.done: every missed deadline or data exception is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Archive the filing package
actions: Upload the submitted form, reconciliation workpaper, sign-offs and HHS confirmation to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by state, market and reporting year.
Confirm the record is retrievable by state and reporting year.
checklist.done: the complete filing package is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by state and reporting year.

testing.step: Build the population of required state/market MLR reports
actions: Extract every state/market combination the issuer wrote business in during the reporting year from the statutory annual statement.
Compare to the filing calendar's list of submitted reports.
List any state/market present in the statutory blank but missing from the filing calendar as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population of required reports is reconciled to the statutory blank with omissions listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Confirm each report was submitted by July 31
actions: Pull the HHS submission confirmation timestamp for each state/market report.
Compare the timestamp to the July 31 statutory deadline.
List any late submission as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every report's submission timestamp is verified against the July 31 deadline.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of state/market reports with a rebate due.
Take a random sample of 8 additional reports from the remainder, minimum 15 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every rebate-due report.

testing.step: Re-perform the reconciliation of reported figures to the statutory blank
actions: For each sampled report, independently trace premium, claims and expense figures back to the statutory annual statement exhibits.
Recompute the variance percentage; anything beyond the procedure's tolerance is a fail.
Capture the recomputation into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled report's figures are independently reconciled to the statutory blank with the threshold applied.

testing.step: Verify actuarial and Controller sign-offs predate submission
actions: Confirm the Appointed Actuary and Controller sign-off dates on each sampled report predate the HHS submission timestamp.
Confirm the compliance review sign-off is also present and dated before submission.
List any report missing or out-of-sequence sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: sign-off sequencing is confirmed correct for every sampled report.

testing.step: Recompute the rebate calculation and distribution for sampled rebate-due reports
actions: Independently recompute the per-enrollee rebate from the certified MLR figures.
Compare to the amount actually distributed by Billing Operations and confirm the distribution date is on or before September 30.
Flag any variance in amount or a late distribution as a compliance exception, not merely a documentation gap.
testing.done: rebate amount and distribution timing are independently verified for every sampled rebate-due report.

testing.step: Trace the submission to the HHS confirmation record
actions: Confirm the saved HHS confirmation number and timestamp exist for each sampled report.
Compare the confirmed data fields to what is on the internal workpaper to confirm no last-minute alteration occurred.
Capture the confirmation screen into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled report traces to a matching, unaltered HHS confirmation record.

testing.step: Check any amended report was properly re-reviewed
actions: For any sampled report that was later amended, confirm the amendment went through actuarial, Controller and compliance review before resubmission.
Confirm any rebate recalculation and reissuance was completed.
Note any amendment that skipped review as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled amendment is confirmed to have been re-reviewed and any rebate impact reissued.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the state/market and what failed.
Assign root cause (data gap, missed deadline, miscalculated rebate) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for missed deadlines, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and self-report assessment where applicable.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and report to the Compliance Committee.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and file it in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

In-scope systems.value: Provider directory and network data sourced from the provider contracting system; network adequacy analysis run against CMS's published standards

Compliance procedure documented.value: Network Adequacy Monitoring Procedure — provider data refresh, time/distance testing, gap identification, remediation, QHP attestation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Network adequacy templates due with the annual QHP certification/recertification submission window (spring, ahead of the plan year)

checklist.step: Refresh the provider directory extract for every QHP service area
actions: Pull the current in-network provider list by specialty, address and service area from the provider contracting system.
Confirm each provider record carries an active contract status and accepting-new-patients flag.
Ask the Data Quality Analyst to run a duplicate/stale-record check on the extract before testing begins.
checklist.done: a cleaned, current provider directory extract exists for every QHP service area.

checklist.step: Run the CMS time/distance test by specialty and county
actions: Load the provider extract into the network adequacy analysis tool and apply the current CMS time/distance thresholds by specialty type and county designation (large metro, metro, micro, rural, CEAC, extreme access).
Compute the percentage of enrollees within the threshold for each specialty/county combination.
List every combination failing the threshold on a gap-tracking sheet.
checklist.done: time/distance results are computed for every specialty/county combination with failures listed on the gap-tracking sheet.

checklist.step: Run the appointment-wait-time and provider-to-enrollee ratio checks
actions: Where the state or CMS standard includes appointment wait-time requirements, sample provider offices and confirm wait times against the standard via the credentialing team's provider survey.
Compute provider-to-enrollee ratios for primary care and behavioral health where applicable and compare to the standard.
Add any ratio or wait-time failure to the gap-tracking sheet.
checklist.done: wait-time and ratio checks are completed with failures added to the gap-tracking sheet.

checklist.step: Investigate and close provider network gaps
actions: For each gap, work with network contracting to add a provider in the deficient specialty/county or extend an existing provider's service area.
Where a new contract cannot be executed before the certification deadline, document the good-faith contracting effort (letters sent, providers contacted, dates).
Update the gap-tracking sheet with the closure date or the good-faith effort documentation.
checklist.done: each gap is closed with a new contract or documented as a good-faith effort with supporting correspondence.

checklist.step: Prepare an exception request for any gap that cannot be closed
actions: Draft an access-plan/exception narrative for each unclosed gap describing alternative access arrangements (telehealth, out-of-network coverage at in-network cost-share, single-case agreements).
Attach the good-faith contracting evidence to the exception request.
Route the exception request to the Head of Compliance for review before submission.
checklist.done: every unclosed gap has a documented exception narrative with supporting evidence, routed for review.

checklist.step: Obtain Head of Compliance sign-off on remediation and exceptions
actions: Review the gap-tracking sheet, remediation actions and exception narratives.
Approve or reject each exception request, documenting the rationale.
Sign off that the network adequacy package is ready for the QHP certification submission.
checklist.done: the Head of Compliance has signed off on remediation actions and every exception decision.

checklist.step: Complete the network adequacy template for QHP certification
actions: Populate the CMS or state network adequacy template with the final provider directory extract and test results.
Attach the exception narratives for any approved exceptions.
Cross-check every field against the underlying test data before finalizing.
checklist.done: the network adequacy template is complete and every field ties to the underlying test data.

checklist.step: Submit the network adequacy template with the QHP certification package
actions: Attach the completed network adequacy template to the QHP certification/recertification submission.
Submit within the CMS certification window and save the submission confirmation.
Log the submission date and confirmation on the QHP certification tracker.
checklist.done: the network adequacy template is submitted with the QHP package and a confirmation is logged.

checklist.step: Publish the provider directory to the public-facing site accurately
actions: Confirm the certified network's provider list is published to the customer-facing provider directory before open enrollment.
Set the required update cadence (no less than monthly per CMS accuracy standards) and confirm the refresh job runs on schedule.
Spot-check a sample of published entries against the source contracting system for accuracy.
checklist.done: the public provider directory reflects the certified network and refreshes on the required cadence.

checklist.step: Monitor mid-year network changes for material adequacy impact
actions: Track provider terminations and contract non-renewals throughout the plan year.
Re-run the time/distance test for any county/specialty losing a provider that could breach the threshold.
Open a new gap-tracking entry for any breach identified mid-year.
checklist.done: mid-year provider losses are monitored and re-tested, with any new breach tracked as a gap.

checklist.step: Issue continuity-of-care notices for material network changes
actions: Where a provider termination affects enrollees in active treatment, generate the continuity-of-care notice required by the state/CMS standard.
Deliver the notice within the required timeframe and log the delivery date per enrollee.
File the notice log with the network adequacy evidence.
checklist.done: continuity-of-care notices are generated, delivered within the required timeframe and logged.

checklist.step: Escalate any service area unable to meet the standard before the deadline
actions: At the T-15 checkpoint, review any service area still failing the standard with no approved exception.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance and Chief Compliance Officer with options: further contracting effort, exception filing, or service-area withdrawal.
Record the decision and owner on the gap-tracking sheet.
checklist.done: every unresolved service area is escalated with a recorded decision before the certification deadline.

checklist.step: Log any certification submitted without a closed or approved-exception gap
actions: Open a tracker issue for any gap that remained open and unexcepted at submission.
Assign root cause and owner and route to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report assessment.
Set a remediation date and track to closure.
checklist.done: every unresolved gap at submission is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Reconcile the final network adequacy evidence set
actions: Confirm the provider extract, test results, gap-tracking sheet and exception approvals are all consistent as of the submission date.
Resolve any inconsistency before archiving.
Confirm the Head of Compliance sign-off is attached to the final set.
checklist.done: the final evidence set is internally consistent and carries the Head of Compliance sign-off.

checklist.step: Archive the network adequacy package
actions: Upload the provider extract, test results, gap-tracking sheet, exception narratives and submission confirmation to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the certification-cycle-plus-6-years retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by service area and plan year.
checklist.done: the complete network adequacy package is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by service area and plan year.

testing.step: Build the population of QHP service areas subject to network adequacy testing
actions: Extract every QHP service area certified for the plan year from the QHP certification tracker.
Reconcile the count to the network adequacy templates submitted.
List any service area missing a submitted template as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population of service areas is reconciled to submitted templates with omissions listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Reconcile the provider directory extract to the contracting system of record
actions: Pull a fresh provider extract directly from the contracting system for a sample of service areas.
Compare provider counts by specialty to the extract used in the original testing.
Flag any material discrepancy as an exception.
testing.done: the provider extract is independently reconciled to the contracting system for the sample.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of service areas with any approved exception.
Take a random sample of 6 additional service areas from the remainder, minimum 10 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every service area with an approved exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the time/distance test for sampled service areas
actions: Independently rerun the time/distance calculation for each sampled specialty/county combination using the CMS-published thresholds.
Compare results to the original test output; any variance in pass/fail outcome is a fail.
Capture the recomputation into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled specialty/county combination has an independent re-performance with pass/fail outcomes compared.

testing.step: Verify exception approvals against the underlying good-faith evidence
actions: For each sampled exception, review the good-faith contracting correspondence and confirm it supports the narrative filed.
Confirm the Head of Compliance approval predates the QHP certification submission.
Flag any exception lacking adequate supporting evidence.
testing.done: every sampled exception is verified against supporting evidence and a predating approval.

testing.step: Confirm continuity-of-care notices were issued where required
actions: For sampled service areas with a mid-year provider termination, confirm a continuity-of-care notice was generated and delivered within the required timeframe.
Trace delivery to the notice log with per-enrollee delivery dates.
Flag any missed or late notice as an exception.
testing.done: continuity-of-care notice issuance is confirmed for every sampled mid-year termination.

testing.step: Verify the public provider directory matches the certified network
actions: Pull a snapshot of the published provider directory for sampled service areas.
Compare to the certified network's provider list from the submission.
Flag any provider listed inaccurately (terminated but still shown, or missing) as an exception.
testing.done: the public directory is verified against the certified network for every sampled service area.

testing.step: Trace the submission to the QHP certification confirmation
actions: Confirm the saved QHP certification submission confirmation exists for each sampled service area.
Compare the submitted template fields to the internal workpaper to confirm consistency.
Capture the confirmation record into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled service area traces to a matching, consistent certification confirmation record.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the service area and what failed.
Assign root cause (stale provider data, unsupported exception, missed notice, directory inaccuracy) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next year's certification as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the pass/fail threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and report to the Compliance Committee.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and file it in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Pull the current Marketplace CSR eligibility file
actions: Retrieve the current 834 enrollment/eligibility transaction feed from the Marketplace, filtering to silver-tier QHP enrollees with a CSR eligibility category (73/87/94/limited cost-sharing).
Confirm the feed is the latest reconciled version, not a stale prior cycle.
Load the eligibility file into the reconciliation workpaper, one row per enrollee.
checklist.done: the current CSR eligibility file is loaded into the workpaper for every silver-tier enrollee.

checklist.step: Pull the policy admin CSR variant extract
actions: In the policy admin system, run the CSR variant report showing each silver-tier enrollee's assigned plan variant and cost-sharing parameters (deductible, copay, MOOP).
Export the extract for the same enrollee population and period as the Marketplace file.
Confirm the extract carries the enrollee's HIOS ID / subscriber ID for matching.
checklist.done: the policy admin CSR variant extract is exported with matching enrollee identifiers.

checklist.step: Match and compare the two data sets
actions: Match Marketplace eligibility rows to policy admin rows by HIOS ID/subscriber ID.
Compare the CSR eligibility category on the eligibility file to the assigned plan variant in policy admin.
Flag every mismatch, every unmatched Marketplace row, and every policy admin row with no corresponding Marketplace eligibility.
checklist.done: every enrollee is matched and compared, with mismatches and unmatched rows flagged.

checklist.step: Validate the cost-sharing parameters for each matched variant
actions: For each matched enrollee, compare the deductible, copay/coinsurance and MOOP configured in policy admin to the CMS-published cost-sharing reduction schedule for that variant.
Flag any configured parameter that does not match the published schedule.
Cross-check against 45 CFR 156.130's cost-sharing standards for the applicable metal tier.
checklist.done: cost-sharing parameters are validated against the CMS schedule for every matched enrollee, with mismatches flagged.

checklist.step: Investigate flagged breaks
actions: For each flagged enrollee, research whether the break is a timing lag (recent eligibility change not yet processed), a data-entry error, or a system configuration issue.
Classify each break and record the classification on the workpaper.
Escalate any pattern affecting more than a handful of enrollees to the Valuation Actuary.
checklist.done: every flagged break is investigated, classified and any pattern escalated.

checklist.step: Correct the policy admin CSR assignment for confirmed breaks
actions: Update the enrollee's plan variant and cost-sharing parameters in policy admin to match the confirmed Marketplace eligibility.
Apply the correction with the correct effective date so retroactive claims can be reprocessed if needed.
Log the correction (before/after values, effective date, correcting user) on the break log.
checklist.done: every confirmed break is corrected in policy admin with the correction logged.

checklist.step: Reprocess claims affected by retroactive CSR corrections
actions: Identify claims paid at the wrong cost-sharing level during the period the enrollee's variant was misconfigured.
Recalculate the correct member cost-share and issuer-paid amount and reprocess/adjust the claim.
Issue any resulting refund or additional billing to the enrollee per the standard claims-adjustment process.
checklist.done: claims affected by the correction window are identified, reprocessed and any member refund/billing issued.

checklist.step: Quantify the CSR advance-payment impact from corrections
actions: Estimate the change in CSR value delivered resulting from the corrections, for use in the next CSR advance-payment true-up.
Document the estimate methodology and the affected enrollee count.
Hand the estimate to Regulatory Reporting for the next CMS CSR reconciliation submission.
checklist.done: the CSR advance-payment impact of corrections is estimated, documented and handed to Regulatory Reporting.

checklist.step: Reconcile unmatched Marketplace eligibility rows
actions: For every Marketplace eligibility row with no policy admin match, confirm whether the enrollee was ever enrolled, is a duplicate, or reflects an enrollment processing delay.
Process any missed enrollment or correct any duplicate.
Log the resolution on the workpaper.
checklist.done: every unmatched Marketplace row is resolved and logged.

checklist.step: Reconcile unmatched policy admin rows
actions: For every policy admin CSR-variant row with no Marketplace eligibility match, confirm whether the enrollee's eligibility was terminated and policy admin was not updated.
Correct the plan variant to standard silver where CSR eligibility has lapsed, effective the correct termination date.
Log the resolution on the workpaper.
checklist.done: every unmatched policy admin row is resolved and logged.

checklist.step: Obtain Valuation Actuary sign-off on the quarterly reconciliation
actions: Review the match rate, break count, corrections made and any unresolved items.
Confirm the break rate is within the procedure's tolerance or escalate if not.
Sign off on the quarterly reconciliation workpaper.
checklist.done: the Valuation Actuary has signed off on the quarterly reconciliation with the break rate assessed.

checklist.step: Feed the reconciled data into the annual CSR data submission
actions: Aggregate the four quarters' reconciled CSR variant and cost-sharing data for the annual CMS CSR reporting cycle.
Confirm the aggregated data is consistent with the EDGE server risk-adjustment/CSR submissions for the same period.
Hand the reconciled package to Regulatory Reporting ahead of the September 30 submission deadline.
checklist.done: the annual CSR data package is aggregated, cross-checked and handed off ahead of the September 30 deadline.

checklist.step: Escalate systemic configuration issues
actions: Where breaks trace to a systemic policy admin configuration defect (e.g., wrong cost-sharing table mapped to a plan ID), escalate to IT and the Head of Compliance.
Track the defect fix through to deployment and re-test the affected population once resolved.
Record the defect, fix date and re-test result on the workpaper.
checklist.done: systemic configuration defects are escalated, fixed and re-tested with the outcome recorded.

checklist.step: Log any break unresolved past one billing cycle
actions: Open a tracker issue for any break not corrected within one billing cycle of identification.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Escalate breaches open beyond two cycles to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every break unresolved past one billing cycle is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Archive the quarterly reconciliation package
actions: Upload the eligibility file, policy admin extract, comparison, break log and sign-off to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by quarter.
Confirm the record is searchable by enrollee and quarter.
checklist.done: the complete reconciliation package is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by enrollee and quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of silver-tier CSR-eligible enrollees for the quarter
actions: Independently extract the Marketplace eligibility file and the policy admin CSR variant extract for the tested quarter.
Reconcile row counts between the two independent extracts and the population used in the original reconciliation.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the tested population is independently extracted and reconciled to the original reconciliation's population.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the CSR advance-payment submission
actions: Compare the enrollee count and CSR variant mix to the corresponding CMS CSR advance-payment/EDGE submission for the same period.
Investigate and document any material difference.
List unresolved differences as exceptions.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the CMS submission with differences investigated.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of enrollees flagged as a break in the original reconciliation.
Take a random sample of 25 additional enrollees from the matched population, minimum 40 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every enrollee flagged as a break.

testing.step: Re-perform the CSR variant match for the sample
actions: Independently match each sampled enrollee's Marketplace eligibility category to their policy admin plan variant.
Compare the result to the original reconciliation's conclusion for that enrollee.
Any disagreement is a fail, logged in the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled enrollee has an independent re-performed match with disagreements logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the cost-sharing parameter validation
actions: For each sampled enrollee, independently compare configured deductible, copay/coinsurance and MOOP to the CMS-published cost-sharing reduction schedule.
Flag any parameter mismatch not already captured in the original reconciliation.
Record the comparison in the test workpaper.
testing.done: cost-sharing parameters are independently re-validated for every sampled enrollee.

testing.step: Trace corrected breaks to policy admin and claims reprocessing
actions: For each sampled break that was corrected, confirm the policy admin record reflects the corrected variant with the right effective date.
Confirm affected claims were identified and reprocessed at the corrected cost-sharing level.
Confirm any member refund or additional billing was issued.
testing.done: corrected breaks are traced through policy admin and claims reprocessing to completion.

testing.step: Recompute the break rate and compare to tolerance
actions: Compute the break rate from the independently re-performed sample.
Compare to the procedure's stated tolerance and to the rate reported in the original reconciliation sign-off.
Flag a material understatement of the break rate in the original sign-off as a finding.
testing.done: the break rate is independently recomputed and compared to tolerance and to the original sign-off.

testing.step: Verify unmatched-row resolution
actions: For a sub-sample of unmatched Marketplace and policy admin rows, confirm the documented resolution is supported by evidence (enrollment record, termination date).
Flag any resolution lacking supporting evidence.
Record findings in the test workpaper.
testing.done: unmatched-row resolutions are verified against supporting evidence for the sub-sample.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date

checklist.step: Classify the inquiry and confirm the applicable citation

Note the citation and provision text on the tracker entry.
checklist.done: the inquiry is classified against a specific, re-verified citation.

checklist.step: Gather the underlying data and workpapers relevant to the inquiry

Extract the specific figures or records the regulator is asking about.
Cross-check the extracted figures against the source system before including them in the draft response.
checklist.done: the specific data the inquiry asks about is pulled and cross-checked against source.

checklist.step: Draft the technical response
actions: Write a direct answer to each question the regulator asked, referencing the specific workpaper and citation.
Avoid volunteering information beyond the scope of the question.
Attach supporting exhibits (extracts, calculations) referenced in the response.
checklist.done: a draft response answers each question directly with supporting exhibits attached.

checklist.step: Route the draft for Regulatory Counsel review
actions: Review the draft for any statement that could constitute an admission of non-compliance and confirm the framing is accurate and defensible.
Confirm no privileged material is inadvertently included.
Approve the draft or return with required edits.
checklist.done: Regulatory Counsel has reviewed and approved the draft before it is finalized.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary sign-off on technical accuracy
actions: Review the final draft's actuarial statements and figures for accuracy.
Confirm the response is consistent with the certified workpapers it references.
Sign off before submission.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has signed off on the technical accuracy of the final response.

checklist.step: Submit the response through the regulator's designated channel
actions: Submit the response through the same channel the inquiry arrived on (SERFF objection response, CMS portal message, formal letter) before the stated deadline.
Save the submission confirmation or delivery receipt.
Update the tracker entry with the submission date and confirmation reference.
checklist.done: the response is submitted through the correct channel before the deadline with a saved confirmation.

checklist.step: Track any regulator follow-up question

Log any follow-up as a linked tracker entry referencing the original inquiry.
Route the follow-up through the same drafting/review/sign-off chain.
checklist.done: any follow-up is logged, linked to the original inquiry and routed through the same review chain.

checklist.step: Escalate any inquiry suggesting a broader compliance gap

Track the internal review to closure independently of the inquiry response.
checklist.done: any inquiry suggesting a broader gap triggers a separate internal review with a self-report assessment.

checklist.step: Escalate any inquiry at risk of missing its deadline

checklist.done: every at-risk inquiry is escalated with a recorded outcome before the deadline.

checklist.step: Close the tracker entry once the regulator confirms receipt or the matter is resolved

checklist.done: the tracker entry is set to Closed with a full correspondence trail attached.

checklist.step: Review closed inquiries quarterly for recurring themes

testing.done: the archive is confirmed complete and retention-labelled for every sampled inquiry.

Match each event to a generated and delivered notice on the notice log.
List any event without a matching notice for immediate investigation.
checklist.done: trigger events are reconciled weekly to the notice log with unmatched events investigated immediately.

checklist.step: Investigate and remediate any missed notice found in the weekly reconciliation
actions: Determine the root cause of the missed notice (workflow rule gap, data error, vendor failure).
Generate and deliver the missed notice as soon as identified, noting the delay on the log.
Fix the root cause so the same trigger type does not recur.
checklist.done: every missed notice found is remediated with a documented root cause and a fix to prevent recurrence.

checklist.step: Report notice delivery performance monthly
actions: Compute the on-time delivery rate against the statutory timeframe for the month's trigger events.
Present the rate and any missed-notice remediation status to the Head of Compliance.
Track the rate trend month over month.
checklist.done: an on-time delivery rate is computed, reported to the Head of Compliance and trended monthly.

checklist.step: Update notice templates when CMS revises required content
actions: Monitor CMS guidance for changes to required CSR/EHB notice content or timing.
Update the notice template and the trigger-event catalog to reflect the change.
Route the updated template through Regulatory Counsel review before it goes live.
checklist.done: notice templates and the trigger catalog are updated and counsel-reviewed whenever CMS revises requirements.

checklist.step: Escalate any systemic delivery failure
actions: Where the monthly on-time rate falls below the internal target, convene the Policy Admin Ops Lead and IT to identify the systemic cause.
Approve a remediation plan and, where a population of enrollees was affected, approve a bulk corrective mailing.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether a self-report is warranted.
checklist.done: any systemic delivery failure triggers a remediation plan, corrective mailing where needed, and a self-report assessment.

checklist.step: Log every notice missed or delivered outside the timeframe
actions: Open a tracker issue for each missed or late notice with the enrollee identifier, trigger event and delay.
Assign root cause and owner and set a remediation date.
Confirm closure once the notice is delivered and logged.
checklist.done: every missed or late notice is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and confirmed closure.

checklist.step: Archive the quarterly notice log
actions: Upload the quarter's notice log, delivery confirmations and reconciliation workpaper to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label and index by enrollee and quarter.
Confirm the record is searchable by enrollee and trigger event type.
checklist.done: the quarterly notice log is archived, retention-labelled and searchable by enrollee and trigger event type.

testing.step: Build the population of CSR-relevant trigger events for the quarter
actions: Independently extract every catalogued trigger event processed in policy admin during the quarter.
Reconcile the count to the weekly reconciliation workpapers produced during the quarter.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population of trigger events is independently extracted and reconciled to the weekly reconciliations.

testing.step: Match every trigger event to a generated and delivered notice
actions: Match each trigger event to a notice log entry with a generation date and delivery confirmation.
List every unmatched trigger event as an automatic exception.
Compute the overall match rate for the quarter.
testing.done: every trigger event is matched to a notice or listed as an exception, with a computed match rate.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of trigger events logged as a missed or late notice.
Take a random sample of 25 additional matched notices, minimum 40 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every missed or late notice.

testing.step: Recompute delivery timeliness for the sample
actions: For each sampled notice, recompute the elapsed time from the trigger event date to the delivery confirmation date.
Compare to the statutory/CMS-guidance timeframe for that notice type; any breach is a fail.
Capture the recomputation into the test workpaper.
testing.done: delivery timeliness is independently recomputed and compared to the required timeframe for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Verify notice content accuracy against the trigger event data
actions: For each sampled notice, compare the CSR variant, effective date and cost-sharing summary stated in the notice content snapshot to the actual trigger event data in policy admin.
Flag any content inaccuracy as a fail.
Record the comparison in the test workpaper.
testing.done: notice content is independently verified against the trigger event data for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Trace delivery confirmations to the print/mail vendor system
actions: For each sampled notice, pull the underlying delivery confirmation record directly from the print/mail or electronic delivery vendor system.
Confirm it matches the confirmation logged in policy admin.
Flag any notice logged as delivered with no corresponding vendor record.
testing.done: delivery confirmations are traced to the vendor system of record for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Verify undeliverable-notice follow-up was completed
actions: For sampled notices originally returned undeliverable, confirm address research, re-issue and any required escalation occurred within the procedure's timeframes.
Flag any undeliverable notice with no documented follow-up.
Record the finding in the test workpaper.
testing.done: undeliverable-notice follow-up is verified for every applicable sampled notice.

testing.step: Verify remediation of any prior-identified missed notice
actions: Pull all missed/late-notice tracker issues opened in the quarter.
Confirm each carries a root cause, owner, remediation date and evidence the notice was ultimately delivered.
Flag any issue open past its remediation date without escalation.
testing.done: every missed-notice tracker issue is confirmed remediated or flagged if overdue without escalation.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the enrollee identifier, trigger event and what failed.
Assign root cause (workflow gap, vendor failure, content error, address issue) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and the on-time delivery rate against the pass/fail threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and report to the Compliance Committee.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and file it in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and on-time delivery rate is filed and reported.
